messages:
Marie (Sales): Hey team — Acme is on the hook to finish the SIG CAIQ follow-up. Key asks: RTO/RPO for Hosted vs Dedicated, backup cadence, failover flow, test cadence and where we can point them for artifacts. They want something concise for procurement by EOD Thu. @Jordan @Claire :hourglass:
Jordan (Eng-SRE): @Marie quick q — are they evaluating Hosted API only or requesting Dedicated/Private pricing? RTO/RPO differ a lot by deployment.
Marie (Sales): They're primarily evaluating Dedicated for production but asked for Hosted comparatives too. Can we put both in one response? Keep it short, one A4.
Claire (Security): We can do a one-pager. Topline: Dedicated has SLA-backed availability and explicit failover runbooks; Hosted is multi-region with operational DR but no reserved capacity SLA. I'll draft control statements and link to artifacts. Need the numeric targets from infra.
Neil (Infra): Drafting numbers now. Rough summary to confirm:
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): contractual uptime 99.9%+, automated intra-region failover within <5m for node-level issues; full-region failover <60m for primary->secondary region with our cross-region replication. RPO: <15m for control-plane metadata; customer data snapshots daily by default, optional hourly snapshot for enterprise add-on (configurable).
- Hosted (shared pool): designed for low-latency multi-AZ serving; for regional outage we failover traffic to the nearest healthy region. Observed median region failover time ~10-45m depending on warm capacity; we do not offer contractual RTO for self-serve hosted. RPO for customer persisted artifacts is 24h by default.
Marie (Sales): Nice. Can you also confirm backup retention and encryption notes? They asked about backups, restore testing, and KMS/HSM usage.
Claire (Security): Backups: encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS for Private or our managed KMS for Hosted/Dedicated (AES-256). Retention: default 30d snapshots; longer retention available as add-on. We perform quarterly restore drills of a representative subset of customer snapshots; annual full DR exercises for Dedicated customers (can provide table of last 3 test dates on request). :white_check_mark:
Jordan (Eng-SRE): Adding runbook excerpt for failover path (will paste below). Keep in reply as code block in the one-pager.
Neil (Infra): Runbook snippet:
```
1) Detect outage via routing/health checks (automated).
2) Promote warm secondary: enable routing -> update DNS TTL -> shift traffic to secondary region.
3) Validate KV/store consistency, warm caches, run smoke tests.
4) Monitor for error >5% -> scale capacity / trigger on-call.
5) Post-mortem & snapshot of primary state when available.
```
Claire (Security): Also call out access controls during failover: RBAC enforced, emergency break-glass audit log, and signed change records stored in immutable log. Mention SOC2/HIPAA controls where relevant.
Alex (Sales-ops): I'll assemble the one-pager and attach the links. Can someone drop links to the supporting artifacts (latest DR test report, snapshot policy doc, SLA doc) and a redacted example of a restore report we can share with procurement?
Jordan (Eng-SRE): Links:
- SLA & uptime: https://redwood.example.com/legal/sla
- Snapshot & backups: https://redwood.example.com/docs/backups
- DR test summary (redacted): https://redwood.example.com/internal/dr-tests/2025-q1-redacted
Claire (Security): I'll PM a redacted restore report PDF. Note: we should avoid sharing internal credentials; deliverables will be redacted.
Marie (Sales): Dream team, thanks. Alex & I will finalize and send to Acme. If procurement asks for formal attestation, flag me and we'll route to legal. :pray:
